title: Lactate threshold concepts: how valid are they?
authors: Faude O, Kindermann W, Meyer T
population: Review of 25 lactate-threshold concepts and 32 studies relating thresholds to endurance performance
findings: 25 different lactate-threshold concepts were located and divided into three categories: fixed blood-lactate values, first rise above baseline, and breakpoint or MLSS-seeking methods.
32 studies related lactate thresholds to performance in (partly simulated) endurance events; the overwhelming majority reported strong linear correlations, particularly for running events.
There is evidence that some thresholds can estimate the maximal lactate steady state (MLSS), but the variability of individual differences between a threshold and MLSS is rarely reported.
The aerobic-anaerobic transition framework consists of two typical breakpoints: where blood lactate begins to rise above baseline, and the MLSS.
limitations: Published 2009; narrative synthesis; validity judged by correlation with performance and MLSS, with individual-level error rarely available; MLSS has since been questioned as the upper boundary (see Nixon 2021).
implications: Use a two-breakpoint model (LT1: first sustained lactate rise; upper breakpoint) for zone structure rather than a single universal fixed-lactate value.
Because individual threshold-to-MLSS error is unreported, carry an uncertainty band on each threshold and avoid false precision in zone boundaries.

verification.notes: Crossref title 'Lactate Threshold Concepts', vol 39 pp 469-490, matches. Abstract confirms all numbers.
